source.author: Anastasia Kireeva
source.title: Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (problems 36-38)

methods.B1: Changed category to pseudorandomness-plus-smoothing and isolated the missing structural bootstrap from a natural distribution property to the high-degree tail condition; no theorem claim made.
methods.B13: Identified interface/reassembly complexity as the missing monovariant; current pressure, leverage and ratio quantities diagnose spectral cliffs but do not rule them out from low-degree information alone.
methods.B25: Compared the exact two-copy kernel count with the one-copy diagonal leverage count and prioritized cancellation-aware decomposition over further diagonal-envelope refinements; no theorem claim made.

blocker: Need a recognizable distributional/local hypothesis H(P_n,Q_n,T_n,G_n) implying a uniformly bounded source-scale high-degree two-copy/leverage tail at D_n=(log n)^(1+Omega(1)), broad beyond already-covered positive regimes and structurally excluding Mao/Buhai.
prior_art_status: bounded current search through 2026-09-17 found no source-complete general criterion; negative search is not novelty evidence
